newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Energis seeks to be Northeast force.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Energis seeks to be Northeast force.

text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc formed Energis Resources Inc to be one of the top three energy service providers in the U.S. northeast, the chief executive of the new unit told Reuters.
And Enterprise is willing to invest to make that happen, Frank Cassidy said, adding "no significant profits are expected for two or three years."
He said Energis is now generating revenues at an annual rate of about $100 million and expects to top $1 billion within five years.

Cassidy was point man for Enterprise's Public Service Electric & Gas Co utility on the New Jersey Energy Master Plan negotiations with state regulators before being named to head Energis last Fall. In November, he was named head of a unit still to be named that was consolidating functions previously performed by several Enterprise companies, including U.S. Energy Partners and Enterprise Strategic Energy Solutions.
By the time the new unit's name was announced January 30, Energis was providing natural gas to more than 3,600 business clients.
And, it will be filing shortly for a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission power marketing license, Cassidy said.
"The real value we add is packaging services," he said.

It needs a license to be a power buyer to aggregate power to meet the needs of individual customers as the market opens up, he explained, adding Energis has no plans at this time to compete with PSE&G's power marketing activities.
Currently, Cassidy noted, sales under the pilot retail wheeling programs underway in the northeast are being made "below the cost of aggregating" that power.

There will be "a couple of years of (such) cut-throat competition" before there is a shakeout in the energy service business, he said, noting the first to fall will be those who are under capitalized. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
